expectations.text: Output identifies random negative sampling as a key validity problem (easy negatives inflate AUROC by 10-20pp)
expectations.evidence: Random edge splitting creates trivially easy negatives ... This can inflate AUROC by 10–20 percentage points compared to a more realistic evaluation.

expectations.text: Output specifically identifies GNN message-passing leakage: test edges are visible in the message-passing graph during node encoding, so the model effectively 'sees' the test answers while training
expectations.evidence: When you train a GNN on 80% of edges but leave the full graph structure intact for message passing during inference, the model can effectively 'see' the test edges ... node embeddings produced by message-passing are computed using the entire graph, including the test edges you held out.

expectations.text: Output recommends a temporal train/test split (train on edges before time T, evaluate on edges after T) as the correct evaluation for the stated temporal forecasting goal
expectations.evidence: The correct design is a temporal split: train on all edges observed before some cutoff time T, and evaluate on edges that appear after T.

expectations.text: Output recommends comparing to a simple structural baseline (Adamic-Adar, Jaccard, or Common Neighbors) as a required sanity check
expectations.evidence: Required sanity check: structural baselines ... you should compute Adamic-Adar, Jaccard coefficient, and Common Neighbors on your test set.

expectations.text: Output recommends hard negative sampling (distance-2 non-edges or structurally similar non-edges) as a required fix
expectations.evidence: Use hard negatives: non-edges between nodes at distance 2, or within the same community.
